clue.text: Misunderstanding approaching bridge?

definitions.meaning: two parties talking past each other, each with a different aim in mind
read whimsically, someone heading for a bridge is going there for the purpose of crossing it

explanation.surface: A muddle arises as someone heads toward a bridge, or perhaps sits down to the card game.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful second reading: 'bridge' tempts you toward the card game, but here it is a river crossing.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes people with conflicting aims who misunderstand one another, while the literal reading suggests intentions of crossing.

clue.text: Dress queen up in dismay

indicators.note: the reversed queen sits inside the word for dismay

parts.note: to appal is to fill with dismay

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word for queen is read from bottom to top

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the standard abbreviation for the Queen

explanation.surface: The Queen dressing up causes alarm among courtiers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' works because this is a down clue: the queen's letters are read bottom to top. 'Dress' looks like a verb but is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Apparel is clothing, a noun synonym of dress as in formal dress.

clue.text: Circling rock before being smothered by irritant gas

indicators.note: the word for before is wrapped up inside the letters for the gas

parts.note: CS gas is the tear gas used in riot control
ere is a poetic word for before

explanation.surface: Something orbits a rock before being choked by tear gas.
explanation.definitionFit: Ceres is the dwarf planet orbiting in the asteroid belt, a rock circling the Sun.

clue.text: With wealth on view, only let up when it's blown

indicators.note: the words are blown apart and their letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A display of riches only lets up when the money is blown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when it's' is linking; 'blown' signals the anagram of ONLY LET UP.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something opulently means doing it with conspicuous, lavishly displayed riches.

clue.text: Who's in charge of curlers? Bob

definitions.meaning: the captain of a curling team on the ice is called by this short title
to bob is to bounce or hop lightly

explanation.surface: Hair curlers and a bob haircut suggest a visit to the hairdresser.
explanation.walkthrough: Curlers and bob suggest hairdressing; in fact curling is the ice sport where the team captain has this title.
explanation.definitionFit: A skip captains a curling rink, and to skip is to hop along, as to bob does.

clue.text: Exercise quite profitably

parts.note: to exercise a power is to use it
quite in the sense of completely, fully

explanation.surface: Doing exercise turns out to be quite profitable.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something usefully means doing it to good effect, to advantage or profit.

clue.text: Ancient Briton bearing round loopy decoration

indicators.note: the Briton carries the round letter inside him

parts.note: the Picts were an ancient people of northern Britain
a round shape resembles the letter O

explanation.surface: An ancient Briton wears a looped ornament.
explanation.definitionFit: A picot is a small loop of thread forming an ornamental edging on lace or ribbon.

clue.text: Raise new skills to a higher level in port

indicators.note: in a down clue, moving to a higher level means reading the whole run upwards

parts.note: to rear is to raise, as with children
arts are skills, as in the arts of war

explanation.surface: Someone improves their skills while working in a harbour town.
explanation.walkthrough: REAR + N + ARTS read upward gives the answer. STRANRAER is a ferry port in south-west Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Stranraer is a Scottish harbour town that long ran ferries to Northern Ireland.

clue.text: Essayist's written about quiet part of church

indicators.note: the essayist's name is written around the letter for quiet

parts.note: Richard Steele, essayist who co-founded The Spectator; the 's stands for has
P, piano, is the musical direction for quiet

explanation.surface: An essayist has composed a piece about a quiet corner of a church.
explanation.definitionFit: A steeple is the tall tower and spire rising from a church.

clue.text: Dirty film about beautiful boy that's brief ecstasy for prickly type

indicators.note: the film's letters go around the shortened boy

parts.note: porn, short for pornography

indicators.note: a brief version of the word loses its final letter

parts.note: Cupid, the god of love, is pictured as a beautiful winged boy
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A seedy film featuring a pretty boy offers a moment of rapture to a thorny character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's brief' docks the boy's last letter, and 'about' puts the film round him; ecstasy's letter comes last, while 'for' merely links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The porcupine is a rodent covered in sharp quills, so a prickly creature.

clue.text: Dog that's exhibiting measure of radioactivity

parts.note: a cur is a mongrel dog
i.e., id est, means that is

explanation.surface: A dog is found to be giving off radiation.
explanation.definitionFit: The curie is a unit of radioactivity named after Marie and Pierre Curie.

clue.text: Bacon appearing more headstrong

definitions.meaning: a single thin slice of bacon

explanation.surface: Bacon, the philosopher or painter, is seen as more reckless.
explanation.walkthrough: Bacon looks like a name (Francis Bacon) but is the breakfast meat.
explanation.definitionFit: A rasher is one slice of bacon, and rasher is also the comparative of rash, meaning more impetuous.

clue.text: Conclude business well, although at very fast speed

parts.note: but in the sense of yet, although
ton-up is slang for going at a hundred miles an hour

explanation.surface: A deal is closed successfully but at breakneck pace.
explanation.walkthrough: A TON is British slang for 100 mph, so ton-up means speeding.
explanation.definitionFit: To button up a deal is to finish it off and settle it satisfactorily.

clue.text: Member worried papal representative

parts.note: a leg is a limb, a member of the body
ate in the sense of gnawed at, as in what's eating you

explanation.surface: A club member frets about the Pope's envoy.
explanation.definitionFit: A legate is an envoy sent by the Pope with delegated authority.

clue.text: Enjoying friendly relations in later years …

explanation.surface: Two people stay on good terms as they age.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links into the next clue's surface but plays no part in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both being on good terms and becoming elderly.

clue.text: Someone once loved strewing leaf mould around — it's not universal

indicators.note: strewing scatters the letters into a new order
the universal letter is not included, so it is taken away

parts.note: U is the film certificate for universal

explanation.surface: Someone spreads compost about, though it isn't for everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes U from LEAF MOULD, and 'strewing' rearranges what is left; 'around' and 'it's' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: An old flame is a former sweetheart, someone you were once in love with.

clue.text: … after changing, ran off to lake like brothers

indicators.note: the word after is changed into a new arrangement
ran is knocked off into a new order

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for lake on maps

explanation.surface: Following the previous clue, someone changes and runs off to a lake with siblings.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis continues 14-down's surface. 'changing' and 'off' each scramble their own word; the lake's letter ends it, with 'to' as a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Fraternal means brotherly, from the Latin frater for brother.

clue.text: Illegally take flag up a flagstaff?

definitions.meaning: to seize a vehicle or aircraft by force
a jack is a flag, and one hoisted up a pole is high

explanation.surface: Someone steals a flag by running it up a pole.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a variant spelling of hijack, read playfully as a jack flying high.
explanation.definitionFit: To commandeer a plane or lorry by force is the crime named here, spelled in its older variant form.

clue.text: What might be found in tack room, gradually

definitions.text: What might be found in tack room
definitions.meaning: a stable's tack room holds bridles, each with a metal mouthpiece for the horse
slowly, a little at a time

explanation.surface: Things are found in the stable store little by little.
explanation.walkthrough: A tack room is where saddles and bridles are kept; the bit is the mouthpiece of a bridle.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means step by step, and literally pictures horses' mouthpieces lined up one beside another.

clue.text: Attacked in pub, was haemorrhaging excessively internally

indicators.note: the word for excessively is placed inside the word for haemorrhaging

parts.note: bled, lost blood
OTT, over the top

explanation.surface: Someone bleeding heavily inside after a pub fight.
explanation.walkthrough: Being hit with a bottle in a pub brawl is the British sense of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To be struck with a glass bottle in a bar fight is to be bottled in British slang.

clue.text: Capital of African mountain state suffering setback

indicators.note: a setback sends the whole run backwards

parts.note: berg is the South African word for a mountain
AZ is the abbreviation for the US state of Arizona

explanation.surface: An African mountain state is having a difficult time.
explanation.walkthrough: BERG + AZ read backwards gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Zagreb is the capital city of Croatia.

clue.text: Measure devised by the Bard

indicators.note: the letters are devised, worked into a fresh order

explanation.surface: Shakespeare invented a unit of measurement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the Bard' looks like Shakespeare; its letters are the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Breadth is width, a dimension or measurement across something.

clue.text: Time I left island around nightfall

indicators.note: the island's name goes around the two letters

parts.note: the Isle of Wight off the south coast of England

explanation.surface: It is time for me to leave the island as night falls.
explanation.walkthrough: The ISLE OF WIGHT is an island off southern England; IL goes inside it after T.
explanation.definitionFit: Twilight is the dim period of dusk as night falls.

clue.text: In Hajj robe all Muslims have to start with

definitions.text: In Hajj robe all Muslims have to start with

indicators.note: only the starting letter of each word is taken

explanation.surface: All Muslims on the Hajj must first put on a special robe.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening letters of five words spell the answer, and the whole clue also describes it.
explanation.definitionFit: The ihram is the plain white garment pilgrims wear in the sacred state for Hajj.

clue.text: Grass fellow with no right to salvation

indicators.note: the letter for right is removed

parts.note: rescue is salvation from danger

explanation.surface: An informer has no claim to being saved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grass' tempts as British slang for an informer; it is the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Fescue is a genus of tufted grasses used in lawns and pasture.

clue.text: A hundred and four touring island

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

indicators.note: the letters tour around into a new order

explanation.surface: A hundred and four people go touring an island.
explanation.definitionFit: Corfu is a Greek island in the Ionian Sea.

clue.text: Forbidding story teller to talk

indicators.note: talk signals the name is heard spoken

parts.note: the Brothers Grimm collected fairy stories

explanation.surface: A storyteller is forbidden to speak.
explanation.definitionFit: Grim means stern and forbidding in appearance.

clue.text: Beer needs to mature, going from side to side

indicators.note: the word for mature goes from one end marker to the other, sitting between them

parts.note: left and right, L and R
to age is to mature

explanation.surface: Beer must be left to mature, sloshing about.
explanation.walkthrough: AGE runs from L (left) to R (right).
explanation.definitionFit: Lager is a light beer stored to mature, from the German for store.

clue.text: Mullein which produced almonds

definitions.meaning: a tall plant with yellow flower spikes
in the Bible, the staff of Moses' brother budded and bore almonds

explanation.surface: A garden plant is said to have yielded almonds.
explanation.walkthrough: Numbers 17 tells of the staff that blossomed and yielded almonds.
explanation.definitionFit: The plant name is borrowed from the biblical staff of the high priest, which miraculously bloomed.

clue.text: Bad jokes — come off it (4,4,2,5) 23,212

definitions.meaning: a groaning retort to feeble humour

explanation.surface: Someone groans at poor jokes and tells the joker to stop.
explanation.walkthrough: The trailing 23,212 is the puzzle number caught in the page scan, not part of the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The sarcastic retort greets an unfunny joke, and also expresses scornful disbelief like stop kidding.
